limitations: Most KB images are 8-bit screenshots of ImageJ/areaDetector viewers (display range stretched, often scaled 33-75 %): absolute counts, noise and transmission are NOT recoverable; geometry (widths in px/um, angles, spatial spectra) is. Viewer scale and native frame size were inferred from the window width (canvas = native size x scale + border 10/18/28 px, checked on 13 windows whose title was read by eye), camera from the native size/aspect; pixel sizes then come from the logged um/px of the same era. Measurements are per frame, frames within a log are correlated, so n_logs << n_frames.
provenance: user-log citations are given only as 'user log <year>'; startup/tables documents as doc_id:line. No image or crop is stored here, only derived numbers.

frames.note: viewer scale NOT visible in the title (assumed 50%) -> top width uncertain

pin.methods: Per frame: grey image of the viewer canvas, yellow ROI/cursor pixels inpainted, row-wise pairing of strongest falling/rising gradients (smoothed 1 px), Theil-Sen lines through consistent rows (|resid|<3 px) -> half angle = atan((slopeR-slopeL)/2), tip row = start of the longest consistent run, top width = measured edge separation 4-8 rows below the tip (flat, rounded corners excluded) converted with um/px x 1/viewer scale. Edge 10-90 %: shear-aligned mean profile over rows 60-260 px below the tip.
pin.conclusion: Two pin families in the logs. A: half angle 14.8 +/- 0.25 deg (n=8 frames, 3 independent sessions in this sample), top width 135-220 um. B: half angle 7.8 +/- 0.06 deg (n=3 frames, 1 session), top width 105 um. sim.json uses top 104.5 um together with 15 deg: these belong to different pins; the 104.5 um flat of the test data goes with 7.8 deg.
pin.display_ratio_note: inside/outside grey ratio is a display quantity (unknown min/max stretch): 0.2-0.46 (A), 0.59-0.65 (B); not a transmission.
pin.chord_model_fit: FAILED/not usable: fitting exp(-mu*chord) to the interior profile (background gradient + unknown display offset) gave tau 0.3-12 with relative rms 0.1-0.5; no result retained. The edge softness is used instead (see physics).

physics.note: W K edge 69.525 keV: mu jumps 66 -> 200 /cm between 62 and 71.7 keV. At 71.676 keV a 104.5 um W path transmits 0.12 and sim T=0.08 needs 126 um, the test-frame 0.045 needs 155 um (xraydb, rho 19.3).
physics.edge_width_formula: round pin, chord t(x)=2 sqrt(2 R x) near the silhouette: x10-x90 = ((ln10)^2-(ln(1/0.9))^2)/(8 R mu^2) = 0.661/(R mu^2)  (R half width at that row). mu=200/cm, R=80..140 um: 21..12 um; mu=104/cm (52 keV): 77..44 um; measured group A median 24 um (IQR 20-26, n=14, energy of the frame unknown): the same order, so the edge softness of a thick pin is chord geometry, not detector PSF.

texture.methods: Beam-only frames whose window geometry was identified (viewer scale>=0.5, <5 % display saturation). Footprint = largest connected region >0.4 x p95; inner box = footprint shrunk 18 % per side (>=64 px, >=90 % filled, <15 % masked); cubic polynomial removed; relative residual t = I/fit-1; 2D Hann-windowed autocorrelation; radial ACF fitted at lags 2..60 px (skips the white-noise spike) with A exp(-r/l) or A exp(-r^2/2l^2) (best rms); PSD power-law slope over periods 6-60 screen px.

sim_reference.note: same pipeline on blade.vbl.imaging.beam_texture (amp 0.15, 2 mm field, 8 seeds, 4 um grid)

recommended.action: VBL texture: correlation lengths ~0.37x and rms ~0.27x of the current beam_texture; real frames are streakier (slit-edge / window fringes), not blobby
recommended.bias_note: the radial-ACF estimator (windowed, boxes 0.3-0.9 mm = 12-35 l) underestimates the true 1/e length by 15-30 % (tested on synthetic fields, camera_fit.fit_acf_length_um): true length probably ~32 um; the sim estimate (2 mm field) is biased by ~10 %, so the sim blobs are ~2-2.5x too long

texture.caveats: rms is a display-stretch relative contrast (upper bound of the true relative modulation); frames mixing slit footprint streaks and mottle; fine scales below ~3 screen px are aliased by 33-75 % viewer downsampling.

slit_edges.methods: Footprint edge of beam-only frames (viewer scale>=0.75): mean profile over the central 40 % of the edge, 10-90 % between plateau and background medians.
slit_edges.conclusion: Edges are slit images: median 10-90 % width 38 um (PG, n=63; horizontal edges 32, vertical 48 um) and 19 um (GH1, n=15); minimum 8-10 um. They include geometric penumbra + Fresnel + PSF, so they only bound the PSF (sigma <= ~3 um, 2.6 sigma = 8 um). The sharpest silhouette edge (pin, 2-4 um 10-90 at viewer 75 %) bounds the GH1 PSF sigma <= ~1.1 px (0.8 um) at that pin; sim.json psf_px 1.8 is not contradicted.

dust.methods: dark spots <-max(4 MAD-sigma, 6 %) after dividing by a sigma=6 px Gaussian background, 3-2000 screen px, inside the beam inner box, viewer scale>=0.75
dust.conclusion: ~29 spots/mm^2 of equivalent diameter ~4 um (p90 9 um) at the scintillator; detection-limited (noise/speckle contributes); sim camera_maps gives ~30/mm^2 for pg1 but spots 5-21 um diameter: shrink radius to 1-5 px.
